definitions.explanation: A person who inherits and carries on a family business, household, or tradition. Emphasizes the continuation of a family line or enterprise rather than simply inheriting property.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長男|ちょうなん}→長男：14519_chounan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{跡取|あとと}りだ。
examples.english: The eldest son is the heir to the family.

examples.japanese: {跡取|あとと}りがいなくて、⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{閉|し}める→閉める：00485_shimeru⟧ことになった。
examples.english: With no successor, the shop had to close.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{跡取|あとと}り⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{旅館|りょかん}→旅館：01049_ryokan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{継|つ}いで→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧ほしい⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}っている→思う：00492_omou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{別|べつ}→別：01216_betsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|あゆ}みたい→歩む：13196_ayumu⟧。
examples.english: My father wants me to take over the inn as his successor, but I want to follow a different path.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{跡|あと}→跡：02174_ato⟧ (trace, footsteps) + ⟦{取|と}り→取る：00565_toru⟧ (taking). Literally "one who takes over the footsteps." Strongly associated with family businesses and traditional households.

In traditional Japanese society, the {跡取|あとと}り (usually the eldest son) was expected to inherit the family home, business, and responsibilities. This concept remains relevant today, especially for family-run businesses, farms, and traditional arts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {跡取|あとと}りがいない (there is no successor)
- {跡取|あとと}り⟦{息子|むすこ}→息子：00799_musuko⟧ (heir son)
- {跡取|あとと}り⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧ (succession problem)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{後継者|こうけいしゃ}→後継者：12592_koukeisha⟧: successor (more formal, used for organizations and positions)
- ⟦{相続人|そうぞくにん}→相続人：20815_souzokunin⟧: legal heir (focuses on inheritance of property/assets)
